commonMistakes: Covers both "light (weight)" and "easy (difficulty)" — context decides which.

etymology: Derived from писать ("to write"); the original sense is "something written".
commonMistakes: Mind the irregular genitive plural писем, with a dropped ending.

etymology: Traces to a Proto-Indo-European root meaning "value/worth".
commonMistakes: Distinguish цена ("price") from стоимость ("cost/value").

aspectUsage: Imperfective for repeated/habitual "shooting"; use the perfective выстрелить for a single completed shot.
etymology: Derived from стрела ("arrow"); the original sense is "to shoot an arrow".
commonMistakes: Takes стрелять в + accusative (стрелять в цель = "to shoot at a target").

etymology: Borrowed from French situation, ultimately from Latin situs ("position").
commonMistakes: Distinguish положение (one's standing/circumstances) from ситуация (a concrete situation/event).

aspectUsage: Imperfective for the ongoing process of "becoming"; use the perfective стать for a single completed change.
etymology: The imperfective derivative of стать.
commonMistakes: Takes становиться + instrumental (становиться врачом = "to become a doctor").

etymology: Likely a Turkic borrowing, which came to be used alongside the older Slavic root пёс.
commonMistakes: Distinguish пёс (masculine, somewhat casual) from собака (feminine, the standard neutral word regardless of the dog's sex).

etymology: Traces to a Proto-Indo-European root meaning "shining/white".
commonMistakes: белый флаг is a figurative idiom meaning "surrender".

aspectUsage: Imperfective expressing the state of "standing"; it has no true perfective counterpart (постоять is a related word meaning "to stand for a while").
etymology: A basic verb tracing to a Proto-Indo-European root meaning "to stand".
commonMistakes: стоять в очереди is the standard collocation for "to stand in line".

etymology: Derived from the root of образовать ("to form"); the original sense is "shape/form".
commonMistakes: образ жизни is a standard collocation meaning "lifestyle".

etymology: An item-of-clothing noun possibly related etymologically to платить ("to pay" — cloth once served as currency).
commonMistakes: The plural genitive платьев is regular, but mind the spelling.

etymology: Derived from an archaic уречь ("to prescribe"); the original sense is "an assigned task".
commonMistakes: извлечь урок is a figurative idiom meaning "to learn a lesson".

etymology: Borrowed from English "dollar", ultimately from German Taler.
commonMistakes: After 2-4 the singular genitive доллара is used; after 5+ the plural genitive долларов.

etymology: Borrowed from Latin cliens ("one under protection").
commonMistakes: As an animate noun, its accusative equals its genitive (обслужить клиента).

etymology: Borrowed from English "computer", ultimately from Latin computare ("to calculate").
commonMistakes: "To work at the computer" is работать за компьютером (instrumental + за).

aspectUsage: Perfective for a single completed act of "getting/reaching for something"; use доставать for repeated/ongoing reaching.
etymology: Prefix до- plus an archaic стать ("to reach") — "to reach and take".
commonMistakes: Also used colloquially to mean "to annoy/pester" (Ты меня достал! = "You're driving me crazy").

etymology: Traces to a Proto-Indo-European root meaning "voice/to call".
commonMistakes: подать голос is a figurative idiom meaning "to vote / to voice an opinion".

etymology: Derived from разговаривать ("to converse").
commonMistakes: Distinguish беседа (a formal conversation) from разговор (an everyday conversation) by register.

etymology: к plus an archaic стать ("to suit") — "at a fitting moment".
commonMistakes: кстати говоря is a standard phrase for shifting topic, "by the way".

etymology: Borrowed from Greek krabbatos, meaning "bed/couch".
commonMistakes: Distinguish кровать (the bed frame/furniture) from постель (the bedding/bed as a whole).

aspectUsage: Perfective for a single completed act of "shutting up" (very colloquial/rude). Use затыкаться for repeated/ongoing instances.
etymology: Prefix за- plus an archaic derivative of ткнуться ("to poke/jab") — "to plug one's mouth".
commonMistakes: The imperative заткнись! is very rude — never use it outside close, informal relationships.

etymology: Derived from перевести ("to translate / to transfer").
commonMistakes: Covers both "translation" and "[money] transfer" — context decides which.

aspectUsage: Perfective for a single completed act of "figuring out/sorting out"; use разбираться for the ongoing process.
etymology: Prefix раз- plus a variant of собраться ("to gather") — "to take apart and sort out".
commonMistakes: Takes разобраться в + prepositional (разобраться в проблеме).

etymology: A basic word tracing to a Proto-Indo-European root meaning "nose".
commonMistakes: The special locative form на носу ("right nearby, imminent") is used for "close at hand"; also note idioms like водить за нос ("to deceive someone").

aspectUsage: Imperfective for the ongoing act of "spending [time] / seeing someone off / conducting"; use провести for a single completed instance.
etymology: Prefix про- plus водить ("to lead").
commonMistakes: Polysemous — "to spend time", "to see someone off/escort", "to hold an event" — mind the context.

etymology: Derived from списать ("to copy down").
commonMistakes: Nearly synonymous with перечень ("enumeration"), but список is the more common everyday word.

aspectUsage: Imperfective for repeated/habitual joking; use the perfective пошутить for a single completed joke.
etymology: Derived from шутка ("a joke").
commonMistakes: Takes шутить над + instrumental (шутить над другом = "to tease a friend").

etymology: A basic word tracing to a Proto-Indo-European root meaning "sun".
commonMistakes: The л is silent in pronunciation (солнце is pronounced [so-ntse]).

etymology: когда ("when") plus the indefinite particle -нибудь — "someday".
commonMistakes: Used in questions/conditionals for an indefinite future; in plain positive statements однажды can sound more natural.

aspectUsage: A perfective related word meaning "to wait a little" (delimitative). ждать is the general imperfective "to wait" — not a true aspectual pair.
etymology: Prefix по- plus an archaic годить ("to wait for the right moment").
commonMistakes: The imperative погоди! is a very common everyday way to say "hold on!"

etymology: Borrowed from Italian bambagia ("cotton"); the original reference was to paper made from cotton.
commonMistakes: Normally singular as an uncountable noun, but бумаги (plural) is used for "documents/papers".

etymology: Borrowed from Latin operatio ("a work/operation").
commonMistakes: Covers both "surgical operation" and "[military/financial] operation" — context decides which.

etymology: Derived from звонить ("to ring / to call").
commonMistakes: Note the fleeting vowel that drops in declension (звонок→звонка).

etymology: A basic word tracing to a Proto-Indo-European root meaning "egg".
commonMistakes: Mind the irregular genitive plural яиц.

aspectUsage: Imperfective for repeated/habitual selling; use the perfective продать for a single completed sale.
etymology: Prefix про- plus давать ("to give") — "to hand over and sell".
commonMistakes: Mind the aspect pair продавать (selling, ongoing) versus продать (to complete a sale).

etymology: A nominalized adjective from the future stem of быть ("to be") — "that which is to come".
commonMistakes: This is the neuter form of the adjective будущий ("future") used as a noun, so it declines like an adjective.

aspectUsage: Perfective for a single completed act of entering; use входить for repeated/ongoing entering.
etymology: Prefix во- plus идти ("to go") — "to go into".
commonMistakes: войти в историю is a figurative idiom meaning "to go down in history".

etymology: The plural of некоторый ("some"), used as its own determiner.
commonMistakes: Distinguish некоторый from несколько, which emphasizes a small quantity.

etymology: Derived from покоиться ("to rest/be at peace").
commonMistakes: The short forms спокоен/спокойна/спокойно are commonly used in predicate position.

aspectUsage: Perfective for a single completed act of placing; use класть for repeated/ongoing placing.
etymology: Prefix по- plus an archaic ложить ("to place").
commonMistakes: Note that положить (perfective) and класть (imperfective) have completely different stems — an irregular aspectual pair.

etymology: Derived from the root of ехать ("to go by vehicle"); the original sense is "a line that travels".
commonMistakes: Mind the irregular plural поезда, with a stress shift.

aspectUsage: Imperfective for the ongoing act of "passing through / elapsing"; use the perfective пройти for a single completed pass.
etymology: Prefix про- plus ходить ("to walk") — "to walk past".
commonMistakes: проходить обучение is a figurative collocation meaning "to undergo training".

etymology: Traces to a Proto-Indo-European root meaning "simple/spread out".
commonMistakes: The short forms прост/проста/просто are used in predicate position.

etymology: Derived from an archaic преступить ("to step over/transgress"); the original sense is "transgressing the law".
commonMistakes: Unlike грех (a religious sin), преступление specifically denotes a legal crime.

etymology: Traces to a Proto-Indo-European root meaning "forest/thicket".
commonMistakes: The phrase "в лесу" uses a special second locative form лесу.

aspectUsage: Imperfective expressing an ongoing state of ability. научиться is a related word meaning "to become able to [do something]" — not a true aspectual pair.
etymology: Derived from the root of ум ("intellect") — "to be able through intellect".
commonMistakes: Distinguish уметь (to be able, as a learned skill) from мочь (to be able, situationally).

etymology: An archaic demonstrative determiner tracing to a Proto-Indo-European demonstrative root, surviving today only in fixed expressions.
commonMistakes: Barely used in modern Russian outside the archaic set phrase по сей день ("to this day").

etymology: Derived from родить ("to give birth").
commonMistakes: день рождения is the essential fixed phrase for "birthday".

etymology: Borrowed from French billet; the original sense is "a small slip of paper/note".
commonMistakes: обратный билет refers to the return leg of a round-trip ticket.

etymology: A basic word tracing to a Proto-Indo-European root meaning "to cut".
commonMistakes: The instrumental form is ножом, following the regular hard-stem masculine pattern.

aspectUsage: Perfective for a single completed act of stealing; use красть for repeated/ongoing stealing.
etymology: Prefix у- ("completely") plus красть ("to steal").
commonMistakes: украсть время is a figurative idiom meaning "to steal/waste someone's time".

etymology: Derived from глава ("head/chapter"); the original sense is "at the head / most important".
commonMistakes: самое главное is a standard nominalized phrase meaning "the most important thing".

aspectUsage: Perfective for a single completed act of approaching/suiting; use подходить for repeated/ongoing instances.
etymology: Prefix по- ("approach") plus до- ("reach") plus идти ("to go").
commonMistakes: Covers both "to come closer" and "to suit/fit [a requirement]" — context decides which.

aspectUsage: Imperfective for the ongoing act of watching/monitoring; use the perfective проследить for a single completed act of tracking.
etymology: Derived from след ("footprint"); the original sense is "to follow a trail".
commonMistakes: Takes следить за + instrumental (следить за ребёнком = "to watch over a child").

aspectUsage: Perfective for a single completed act of ending; use заканчиваться for the ongoing process of ending.
etymology: A reflexive derivative of закончить — "to end by itself".
commonMistakes: Don't confuse the intransitive закончиться ("to come to an end") with the transitive закончить ("to finish something").

etymology: Derived from лицо ("person/face"); the original sense is "pertaining to the individual".
commonMistakes: личная жизнь is a standard collocation meaning "private life".

aspectUsage: Imperfective for repeated/habitual receiving; use the perfective получить for a single completed receipt.
etymology: Prefix по- plus an archaic лучати ("to obtain").
commonMistakes: получать удовольствие is a figurative collocation meaning "to enjoy [something]".

aspectUsage: Perfective for a single completed act of "arranging/getting [someone] set up"; use устраивать for repeated/ongoing arranging.
etymology: Prefix у- plus строить ("to build") — "to put together properly".
commonMistakes: устроить скандал is a figurative collocation meaning "to cause a scene".

etymology: Derived from добрый ("good/kind"); the sense is "good/goodness".
commonMistakes: нет худа без добра is a standard proverb meaning "every cloud has a silver lining".

etymology: An adjectivized passive participle of любить ("to love").
commonMistakes: The nominalized use (любимый/любимая = "sweetheart") is also common — distinguish it from the adjective use.

etymology: An adjective derived from полиция ("police"), used as a noun.
commonMistakes: Since it's an adjective-origin noun, it declines like an adjective (hard-stem pattern).

etymology: Borrowed from Chinese chá, having entered Russian via the Silk Road.
commonMistakes: A partitive second genitive form чаю is sometimes used (выпить чаю).

etymology: The adverbial form of ужасный ("terrible").
commonMistakes: Frequently used colloquially as an intensifier meaning "very" (even in a positive sense).

aspectUsage: Imperfective for repeated/habitual buying; use the perfective купить for a single completed purchase.
etymology: Prefix по- plus the imperfective derivative of купить ("to buy").
commonMistakes: Mind the aspect pair покупать (buying, process/habit) versus купить (to complete a purchase).

etymology: Prefix по- plus an archaic добный ("resembling").
commonMistakes: ничего подобного is a strong idiom meaning "nothing of the sort / no way".

etymology: Borrowed from German Stück ("a piece/item").
commonMistakes: Used colloquially as a catch-all word for "thing/business/situation" — mind the broad usage.

aspectUsage: A perfective related word meaning "to become necessary". нуждаться ("to need") takes a different subject structure — not a true aspectual pair.
etymology: Prefix по- plus an archaic надобиться ("to be necessary").
commonMistakes: Takes a dative experiencer (мне понадобится = "I will need [it]").

etymology: The adverbial form of совершенный ("perfect/complete").
commonMistakes: совершенно верно is a standard way to agree, "absolutely right".

aspectUsage: A perfective related word meaning "to go somewhere and come back (round trip)"; its corresponding imperfective is ходить (multidirectional).
etymology: Prefix с- plus ходить ("to walk") — "to go and return".
commonMistakes: сходить implies a completed round trip, unlike пойти (one-way).

etymology: Derived from записать ("to write down").
commonMistakes: Covers both "recording" and "[appointment] booking/registration" — context decides which.

etymology: Negative prefix не- plus большой ("big") — "not very big".
commonMistakes: A somewhat softer/more modest way of saying "not very big" than маленький ("small").

aspectUsage: Imperfective for the ongoing process of dying; use the perfective умереть for a single completed death.
etymology: The imperfective derivative of умереть ("to die").
commonMistakes: умирать от скуки/смеха are figurative idioms meaning "to be bored to death / die laughing".

etymology: Borrowed from French toilette, originally meaning "grooming/dressing".
commonMistakes: Because of its French origin, уборная can be used as a more polite alternative.

etymology: An old Russian word for a peasant man; in modern colloquial speech it now generally means "guy/bloke".
commonMistakes: A very casual slang word — use мужчина in formal contexts.

etymology: где ("where") plus the indefinite particle -то.
commonMistakes: Besides "somewhere", it's also used colloquially to mean "approximately" (где-то в пять часов = "around five o'clock").

aspectUsage: Perfective for a single completed glance; взглядывать (its imperfective) exists but is rare in use.
etymology: Prefix вз- ("upward") plus an archaic глянуть ("to look") — "to raise one's gaze".
commonMistakes: взглянуть denotes a single, brief glance — shorter than посмотреть.

etymology: Prefix о- plus a root related to громадный ("so big it makes noise").
commonMistakes: A stronger degree than большой — closer to "huge/enormous".

aspectUsage: Perfective for a single completed act of disappearing; use пропадать for repeated/ongoing disappearing.
etymology: Prefix про- plus an archaic пасть ("to fall") — "to fall away and vanish".
commonMistakes: пропасть без вести is a standard idiom meaning "to go missing without a trace".

etymology: Derived from зад ("rear/behind"); a vulgar/colloquial word.
commonMistakes: A fairly crude slang word — зад/попа are more appropriate in formal contexts.

aspectUsage: Perfective for a single completed act of finding out/clarifying; use выяснять for repeated/ongoing investigation.
etymology: Prefix вы- plus ясный ("clear") — "to bring into the clear".
commonMistakes: выяснить отношения is a standard idiom meaning "to hash things out / clear the air".

etymology: Derived from угодить ("to please/suit"); the original sense is "in a pleasing way".
commonMistakes: Combined with a question word, угодно forms a generalizing "any-" meaning (кто угодно = "anyone at all").

aspectUsage: Perfective for a single completed act of "acting / enrolling"; use поступать for repeated/ongoing instances.
etymology: Prefix по- plus an archaic ступить ("to step") — "to take a step".
commonMistakes: Covers both "to enroll [in university]" and "to act [in a certain way]" — context decides which.

etymology: Derived from дарить ("to give as a gift").
commonMistakes: Note the fleeting vowel that drops in declension (подарок→подарка).

aspectUsage: Perfective for a single completed act of "calling/summoning"; use вызывать for repeated/ongoing instances.
etymology: Prefix вы- ("out") plus звать ("to call") — "to call out".
commonMistakes: вызвать интерес/подозрение is a figurative collocation meaning "to arouse interest/suspicion".

etymology: Prefix за- plus an archaic кон ("boundary/order") — "a set boundary/rule".
commonMistakes: Distinguish правило (an everyday rule) from закон (a state law).

etymology: A basic word tracing to a Proto-Indo-European root meaning "to bite".
commonMistakes: вооружён до зубов is a figurative idiom meaning "armed to the teeth".

aspectUsage: Perfective for a single completed act of inviting; use приглашать for repeated/ongoing inviting.
etymology: Prefix при- plus an archaic гласить ("to call out").
commonMistakes: пригласить на танец is a standard collocation meaning "to ask [someone] to dance".

etymology: The adverbial form of честный ("honest").
commonMistakes: честно говоря is a frequent discourse marker meaning "honestly speaking".

etymology: A basic word tracing to a Proto-Indo-European root meaning "ear"; its plural уши is irregular.
commonMistakes: The plural уши and genitive ушей diverge substantially from the singular — an irregular paradigm.

etymology: как ("how") plus the indefinite particle -то.
commonMistakes: Mind both senses: как-то раз ("once/one time") and как-то ("somehow/vaguely").

etymology: Traces to a Proto-Indo-European root meaning "limb/part".
commonMistakes: Carries both the "[organization] member" sense and a vulgar body-part euphemism — mind the context.

aspectUsage: Perfective for a single completed act of winning; use выигрывать for repeated/ongoing winning.
etymology: Prefix вы- plus играть ("to play/compete") — "to win through competing".
commonMistakes: выиграть время is a figurative idiom meaning "to buy time".

etymology: Derived from простить ("to forgive").
commonMistakes: просить прощения is the essential standard phrase for "to apologize".

etymology: Borrowed from Greek mousike ("the art of the Muses").
commonMistakes: An uncountable collective noun, used only in the singular.

etymology: Derived from состоять ("to consist/be in a state").
commonMistakes: Besides "state/condition", it also keeps an older sense of "fortune/wealth" (человек с состоянием = "a man of means").

aspectUsage: Perfective for a single completed act of changing; use изменяться for repeated/ongoing change.
etymology: A reflexive derivative of изменить ("to change something") — "to change oneself".
commonMistakes: Don't confuse the intransitive измениться ("to change/become different") with the transitive изменить ("to change something").

etymology: Traces to a Proto-Indo-European root for the numeral "six".
commonMistakes: Like other numerals 5+, it's followed by the genitive plural (шесть часов).

etymology: Derived from грязь ("mud/dirt").
commonMistakes: грязная игра is a figurative phrase meaning "dirty tricks/underhanded play".

etymology: Derived from the root that gave советовать ("to advise"); the original sense is "consultation/advice".
commonMistakes: Carries both "advice" and the historical "[Soviet-era] council" sense — mind the context.

aspectUsage: Perfective for a single completed act of running away. Note that the homonymous imperfective сбегать also has a separate sense: "to make a quick round trip".
etymology: Prefix с- ("away") plus бежать ("to run") — "to run away".
commonMistakes: Mind that сбегать (imperfective) has an entirely different meaning, "to quickly go there and back".

etymology: в plus an archaic нутро ("interior") — an adverb/preposition.
commonMistakes: Don't confuse внутри (static location "inside") with внутрь (direction "into/inward").

etymology: Derived from an archaic сватать ("to arrange a marriage").
commonMistakes: The genitive plural свадеб is regular, but its pattern is easy to forget.

aspectUsage: Perfective for a single completed act of tidying/removing; use убирать for repeated/ongoing tidying.
etymology: Prefix у- ("away") plus брать ("to take") — "to take away".
commonMistakes: Убери руки! is also used as a sharp command, "Hands off!"

etymology: Borrowed from English "boss", ultimately from Dutch baas ("master").
commonMistakes: Distinguish начальник (the more formal "boss/supervisor") from the more colloquial босс.

aspectUsage: A multidirectional, habitual imperfective ("to carry/wear") with no true perfective counterpart (отнести/принести etc. are used depending on context).
etymology: The multidirectional form of нести ("to carry [one way]").
commonMistakes: Distinguish носить (habitual/multidirectional) from нести (a single directed act of carrying).

etymology: A basic word tracing to a Proto-Indo-European root meaning "sea".
commonMistakes: Also note the figurative construction море + genitive (море вопросов = "a sea of questions").

aspectUsage: Perfective for a single completed act of tying/connecting; use связывать for repeated/ongoing instances.
etymology: Prefix с- plus вязать ("to knit/tie").
commonMistakes: Covers both "to tie up (with rope)" and "to knit" — context decides which.

aspectUsage: Perfective for a single completed act of starting; use начинаться for the ongoing process of beginning.
etymology: A reflexive derivative of начать ("to start something") — "to start by itself".
commonMistakes: Don't confuse the intransitive начаться ("to begin [by itself]") with the transitive начать ("to start something").

aspectUsage: Perfective for a single completed act of destroying; use уничтожать for repeated/ongoing destruction.
etymology: Prefix у- ("completely") plus ничто ("nothing") — "to reduce to nothing".
commonMistakes: уничтожить улики/документы is a standard collocation meaning "to dispose of evidence/documents".

aspectUsage: Perfective for a single completed act of informing; use сообщать for repeated/ongoing informing.
etymology: Prefix со- plus общий ("common/shared") — "to share → to inform".
commonMistakes: The common construction is сообщить + dative + о + prepositional (сообщить ему о проблеме).

aspectUsage: Imperfective for repeated/habitual sitting down; use the perfective сесть for a single completed act.
etymology: The imperfective derivative of сесть ("to sit down"), from an archaic root сед- ("to sit").
commonMistakes: Don't confuse садиться (the act of sitting down) with сидеть (the state of sitting).

etymology: The adverbial form of далёкий ("distant").
commonMistakes: Don't confuse the adverb далеко with the adjective далёкий.

aspectUsage: Perfective for a single completed act of sitting down; use садиться for repeated/ongoing instances.
etymology: A basic verb from an archaic root сед- ("to sit").
commonMistakes: Note the figurative collocations сесть в тюрьму ("to go to prison") and сесть за руль ("to get behind the wheel / start driving").

etymology: во plus круг ("circle") — "around".
commonMistakes: Takes вокруг + genitive (вокруг стола = "around the table").

etymology: Borrowed via German Küche, ultimately from Latin coquina ("kitchen").
commonMistakes: Besides "kitchen", it also means "cuisine/cooking style" (домашняя кухня = "home cooking").

aspectUsage: Perfective for a single completed act of coming up with/inventing; use придумывать for repeated/ongoing instances.
etymology: Prefix при- plus думать ("to think") — "to think up".
commonMistakes: Distinguish придумать (to invent, neutral/positive) from выдумать (to make up a falsehood, often negative).

etymology: Traces to a Proto-Indo-European root meaning "one who sits nearby".
commonMistakes: Mind the irregular plural соседи, not the expected *соседы.

aspectUsage: Perfective for a single completed act of proposing/offering; use предлагать for repeated/ongoing instances.
etymology: Prefix пред- plus an archaic ложить ("to place") — "to put forward".
commonMistakes: предложить руку и сердце is a standard idiom meaning "to propose marriage".

etymology: Borrowed from French pistolet, likely from an old Czech firearm name.
commonMistakes: Distinguish ружьё (a rifle/shotgun) from пистолет (a handgun) by size and type.

etymology: Traces to a Proto-Indo-European root meaning "big"; in older Russian it already carried the sense "great".
commonMistakes: Distinguish большой (merely big) from великий (great, qualitatively outstanding).

etymology: Derived from малый ("small"); an affectionate diminutive meaning "little one".
commonMistakes: Has an affectionate tone — use ребёнок in formal contexts.

aspectUsage: Imperfective for repeated/habitual dropping by/entering; use the perfective зайти for a single completed instance.
etymology: The imperfective derivative of зайти.
commonMistakes: заходить на сайт is a modern figurative expression meaning "to visit a website".

aspectUsage: Perfective for a single completed act of agreeing; use соглашаться for repeated/ongoing agreeing.
etymology: Prefix со- plus an archaic гласить ("to say") — "to voice together → to agree".
commonMistakes: Takes согласиться с + instrumental (согласиться с мнением).

etymology: Derived from the root of повести ("to lead"); the original sense is "a lead rein / reason".
commonMistakes: по поводу is a standard fixed preposition phrase meaning "regarding".

etymology: A determiner related to весь ("all"); the original sense is "any/every kind of".
commonMistakes: на всякий случай is the essential standard phrase meaning "just in case".

etymology: Derived from удаться ("to succeed/turn out well").
commonMistakes: Желаю удачи! is the standard phrase for "good luck!"

etymology: A basic word tracing to a Proto-Indo-European root meaning "fire", with a fleeting vowel (огонь→огня).
commonMistakes: играть с огнём is a figurative idiom meaning "to play with fire / take a risk".

aspectUsage: Perfective for a single completed act of meeting/greeting; use встречать for repeated/ongoing instances.
etymology: Derived from the root of встреча ("encounter").
commonMistakes: встретить Новый год is a standard idiom meaning "to see in the New Year".

etymology: Derived from an archaic речь ("to say"); the sense is "speech/words".
commonMistakes: часть речи is the standard grammatical term for "part of speech".

etymology: A basic word tracing to a Proto-Indo-European root meaning "hair"; the singular is rarely used, the plural волосы being standard.
commonMistakes: The singular волос is rarely used; the plural волосы (hair as a whole) is the normal everyday form.

etymology: From Greek phos ("light") plus graphein ("to draw") — "drawing with light".
commonMistakes: Both the clipped indeclinable фото and the full declinable фотография are used.

etymology: не plus уже plus an archaic question particle ли — an interrogative particle expressing strong surprise.
commonMistakes: Nearly synonymous with разве, but неужели carries stronger surprise/shock.

etymology: о- plus an archaic очи ("eyes") plus видный ("visible") — "visible to the eye, evident".
commonMistakes: The neuter short form очевидно is also very commonly used as a sentence-initial adverb ("obviously").

etymology: The adverbial form of крутой ("steep"), which developed a colloquial sense of "awesome/cool".
commonMistakes: Distinguish the literal "steep" sense from the colloquial "cool" sense by context.

etymology: Derived from ум ("intellect").
commonMistakes: Distinguish умный (intellectually smart) from мудрый (wise through experience).

aspectUsage: Imperfective expressing an ongoing state of missing/being bored. соскучиться is a related word meaning "to start missing increasingly" — not a true aspectual pair.
etymology: Derived from скука ("boredom").
commonMistakes: Takes скучать по + dative (скучать по тебе, not "скучать тебя").

etymology: Prefix в- plus an archaic друг ("suddenly", unrelated to the modern word for "friend").
commonMistakes: а вдруг is a colloquial phrase expressing a hypothetical worry, "what if".

etymology: From Old Church Slavonic красьнъ ("beautiful"); the modern word narrowed to mean specifically "red".
commonMistakes: Note that "Red Square" (Красная площадь) owes its name to the old meaning "beautiful", not the color.

aspectUsage: Imperfective for habitual/ongoing lying; use the perfective соврать for a single completed lie.
etymology: A colloquial verb, possibly tracing to a Proto-Indo-European root meaning "to speak".
commonMistakes: Distinguish лгать (literary "to lie") from врать (the frequent colloquial synonym) by register.

aspectUsage: Perfective for a single completed attempt; use пытаться for repeated/ongoing attempting.
etymology: A reflexive derivative of an archaic пытать ("to test").
commonMistakes: Takes попытаться + infinitive (попытаться помочь).

etymology: Derived from гореть ("to burn").
commonMistakes: горячая тема/новость is a figurative phrase meaning "a hot topic".

etymology: Derived from a root related to an archaic стеречь ("to watch over/guard").
commonMistakes: The short forms осторожен/осторожна/осторожно are often used in the warning будь осторожен! ("be careful!").

aspectUsage: Imperfective expressing the ongoing state of being ill; use the perfective заболеть for a single completed onset of illness.
etymology: Derived from боль ("pain").
commonMistakes: A homonymous 3rd-person-only form болит ("[it] hurts") follows a completely different conjugation pattern — don't confuse it with this verb (a person being ill).

etymology: Borrowed from Greek idiotes ("a private/unskilled person"), which developed into an insult.
commonMistakes: A fairly harsh insult — avoid it outside casual joking among friends.

aspectUsage: Perfective for a single completed impersonal event of "being lucky" (dative construction). The corresponding imperfective везти has the same form but a separate "to transport" meaning.
etymology: Prefix по- plus везти ("to carry/transport") — the sense developed to "luck being brought to someone".
commonMistakes: Mostly used only in the 3rd-person singular impersonal (повезло/повезёт), taking a dative experiencer (тебе повезло = "you got lucky").

etymology: An affectionate diminutive of минута ("minute").
commonMistakes: Минутку! is a standard everyday phrase meaning "Just a moment!"

aspectUsage: Imperfective for the ongoing act of "approaching/suiting"; use the perfective подойти for a single completed instance.
etymology: The imperfective derivative of подойти.
commonMistakes: Covers both "to come closer" and "to fit/suit [in size, etc.]" — context decides which.

etymology: Traces to a Proto-Indo-European root meaning "high".
commonMistakes: The short forms высок/высока/высоко are used in predicate position.

etymology: Borrowed from English "show"; an indeclinable neuter noun.
commonMistakes: As a loanword, its form stays the same across all cases.

etymology: A lexicalized neuter short form of больной ("painful"), used as an impersonal predicate.
commonMistakes: Takes больно + dative (мне больно = "it hurts me").

aspectUsage: Perfective for a single completed act of vanishing; use исчезать for repeated/ongoing disappearing.
etymology: Prefix ис- ("out") plus an archaic чезнуть ("to vanish").
commonMistakes: The masculine past form исчез drops the -ну- suffix rather than becoming *исчезнул.

etymology: The adverbial form of трудный ("difficult").
commonMistakes: Note the impersonal construction трудно + dative (мне трудно = "it's hard for me").

aspectUsage: Perfective for a single completed act of creating; use создавать for repeated/ongoing creating.
etymology: Prefix со- ("together") plus an archaic здать ("to form").
commonMistakes: создать впечатление is a figurative collocation meaning "to create an impression".

etymology: Traces to a Proto-Indo-European root shared by "right (correct)" and "right (direction)".
commonMistakes: Distinguish правый (the adjective "right [side]") from the similar-looking short form прав ("[you are] correct") — separate words.

etymology: Derived from предложить ("to propose"); also used as the grammar term "sentence".
commonMistakes: Covers both "proposal" and the grammatical "sentence" — context decides which.

aspectUsage: Imperfective expressing the ongoing state of "existing", with no true perfective counterpart (просуществовать is a related word meaning "to exist for a period of time").
etymology: Prefix су- ("together") plus an archaic щество ("essence").
commonMistakes: существовать is an abstract "to exist" — don't confuse it with жить ("to live", more concrete).

etymology: Derived from боль ("pain").
commonMistakes: Distinguish боль (pain itself) from болезнь (the state of being ill).

etymology: An adjectivized past participle of быть ("to be"); the original sense is "having formerly been".
commonMistakes: The nominalized use (бывший/бывшая = "ex [partner]") is also common — distinguish it from the adjective use.

etymology: A kinship term for "uncle", likely of nursery-word origin; grammatically ends in -я but is masculine.
commonMistakes: A masculine noun that declines like a feminine -я noun (дядя, дяди, дяде...).

etymology: The adverbial form of постоянный ("constant").
commonMistakes: Distinguish всегда (always, absolute) from постоянно (constantly/repeatedly, with a slightly colloquial, often complaining nuance).

etymology: The suppletive superlative form of хороший ("good").
commonMistakes: Distinguish лучше (the comparative adverb/adjective) from лучший (the superlative adjective).

etymology: на plus an archaic пример ("example") — an adverb/discourse marker.
commonMistakes: A frequent sentence-initial/medial discourse marker — note it's set off by commas.

etymology: Derived from знать ("to know"); also nominalized to mean "an acquaintance".
commonMistakes: Covers both the nominalized "acquaintance" and the adjective use (знакомое лицо = "a familiar face") — context decides which.

aspectUsage: Imperfective expressing an ongoing state of suspicion; use the perfective заподозрить for a single completed onset of suspicion.
etymology: Prefix по- plus an archaic дозирать ("to look [at]") — "to look behind → to suspect".
commonMistakes: Takes подозревать + accusative + в + prepositional (подозревать его в обмане = "to suspect him of deceit").

etymology: A collective noun derived from родить ("to give birth"); the original sense is "those who were born [here]".
commonMistakes: The partitive form народу is used colloquially to express quantity.

etymology: An affectionate diminutive of an archaic дед ("grandfather").
commonMistakes: A masculine noun that declines like a feminine -а noun.

aspectUsage: Imperfective expressing an ongoing state of "expecting/waiting", with no true perfective counterpart.
etymology: Prefix о- plus an archaic жидать ("to wait").
commonMistakes: More literary/formal in tone than the everyday ждать ("to wait").

aspectUsage: Imperfective expressing an ongoing state of wishing/desiring; use the perfective пожелать for a single completed expression of a wish.
etymology: Traces to a Proto-Indo-European root meaning "to desire".
commonMistakes: оставляет желать лучшего is a standard euphemism meaning "leaves something to be desired".

etymology: Borrowed from Latin charta ("paper"); polysemous for "map", "[playing] card", and "[credit] card".
commonMistakes: Carries several meanings — "map", "card", "playing card" — mind the context.

etymology: Traces to a Proto-Indo-European root meaning "to follow/track".
commonMistakes: оставить след is also used figuratively, meaning "to leave a [lasting] mark".

etymology: Derived from an archaic обычать ("to accustom").
commonMistakes: Note the contrast between обычный (ordinary) and особый (special).

etymology: Borrowed from French autobus — auto ("self") plus (omni)bus ("for everyone").
commonMistakes: "By bus" is на автобусе (prepositional + preposition на).

etymology: Borrowed from French sérieux, ultimately from Latin serius ("grave/weighty").
commonMistakes: The short forms серьёзен/серьёзна/серьёзно are used in predicate position.

etymology: An ordinal numeral developed from the Proto-Indo-European "three" series.
commonMistakes: An irregular soft-stem ordinal with special endings (третья, третье) — mind the pattern.

aspectUsage: In the copular sense "to be", a stative use with no perfective counterpart.
etymology: The imperfective derivative of явиться ("to appear"), which came to serve as a formal written substitute for быть.
commonMistakes: A formal, written-register expression — быть is more natural in speech.

etymology: Derived from край ("edge").
commonMistakes: в крайнем случае is a standard idiom meaning "as a last resort / worst case".

etymology: Derived from вина ("guilt/fault").
commonMistakes: Distinguish виновный (legally guilty) from виноватый (at fault/feeling guilty in everyday terms) by register.

aspectUsage: Imperfective expressing an ongoing state of "meaning", with no true perfective counterpart.
etymology: Prefix о- plus знак ("sign") — "to mark → to mean".
commonMistakes: Nearly synonymous with значить, but означать carries a more literary/formal tone.

aspectUsage: Perfective for a single completed act of selling; use продавать for repeated/habitual selling.
etymology: Prefix про- plus дать ("to give") — "to give over, to sell".
commonMistakes: Mind the aspect pair продать (completed sale) versus продавать (ongoing process of selling).

etymology: The adverbial form of частый ("frequent").
commonMistakes: Don't confuse частый (the adjective "frequent") with часто (the adverb "often").
